## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want deterministic tests that prove the kill-time power-up supply falls with the campaign level, so the supply curve cannot regress unnoticed.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (and the rules tests where appropriate) with tests that:

- Force the scene RNG so the number of drops over N kills is exact and deterministic at level 1 (matches the current 0.18 rate) and at level 10 (matches 0.05, i.e. at most 30 % of the level-1 rate).
- Prove the level is resolved from the live campaign (`WaveManager.currentLevel()?.level`), i.e. after advancing a level the next kills use the new chance, and an unknown level falls back to level 1.
- Prove the small-asteroid Extra Life roll scales by the same ratio and is unchanged at level 1 (`rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`).
- Prove drop types/weights, the mineral kill-drop rule and timed weapon/power-up effects are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (flat 0.18 roll for every level).
- Assertions are exact and seeded — no statistical/threshold flakiness.
- Coverage includes level 1 identity, level 10 endpoint, mid-run level advance, unknown-level fallback and Extra Life proportionality.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules". Blocks the PlayScene drop-roll feature.

# Interruption seam and hermetic crash-path tests

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Slice:** test-first — this child lands the testable seam plus the interruption/lost-message behaviour that child 2 (checkpointed partial capture) and child 3 (usage/docs) build on.

## Goal

As a **maintainer of the recording tooling**, I want the interruption path to be a testable seam (injected page/fs/clock), so the crash path cannot regress into a raw Playwright stack again.

Today `main()` in `scripts/record-session.mjs` inlines the poll loop and the single post-loop buffer read/write, and only SIGINT/SIGTERM are treated as stops. A `page.waitForTimeout` / `page.evaluate` rejection from a closed page escapes to the top-level handler, prints the raw Playwright message and exits 1 with nothing written and no path named. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` cannot reach any of that without a real browser.

## Scope

- Extract from `main()` and export, fully injectable (page `evaluate`, fs writes, clock):
  - `runRecordingWaitLoop({ evaluate, stop, now, wait, maxDurationMs, pollMs, auto })` → a **stop reason** (`'sigint'`, `'run_end'`, `'max_duration'`, `'target_closed'`), classifying a thrown target-closed failure as `'target_closed'` and consulting `page.isClosed()` / `browser.isConnected()` where available (match the known target-closed message family; any unknown failure defaults to the interruption path, never a raw stack).
  - The interruption finaliser: on `'target_closed'` with nothing captured, print exactly one actionable line naming the resolved output path that was not written plus the Ctrl+C procedure, and return exit code 1. On a clean stop, write the final recording and remove any partial (partial *creation* is child 2; this child makes the removal/salvage decision point exist and be tested).
- New `scripts/record-session.test.ts` (`@vitest-environment node`, temp dirs via `mkdtempSync`, **no real browser**): injected `evaluate`/fs/clock fakes.
- Declare every new export in `scripts/record-session.d.mts`.
- Reuse, do not reimplement: `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` from `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`; mirror the salvage/partial idiom of `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs` and the `<stem>.partial.*` naming of `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The interruption path is covered by hermetic tests.** New tests (`scripts/record-session.test.ts`, node environment, no real browser — page/fs/clock injected) prove: (a) a target-closed error thrown from the poll loop routes to the salvage path and not to a raw error exit; (b) with zero captured bytes the lost message names the output path and the Ctrl+C procedure; (c) a clean stop writes the final file and removes the partial. `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` keeps passing.
2. The wait/finalise logic of `scripts/record-session.mjs` is exported as injectable functions (page `evaluate`, fs writes and clock injected) so the crash, salvage and clean-stop paths are covered hermetically in `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — no real browser in the suite.
3. A target-closed error thrown from the poll loop routes to the interruption/rescue path and never surfaces a raw Playwright target-closed message as the only diagnostic; the process exits non-zero.
4. With zero captured bytes the recorder prints exactly one actionable line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was not written; proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`.
5. On a clean stop the final recording is written and no partial file remains, proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`.
6. `scripts/record-session.d.mts` declares every newly exported helper and the type check passes.
7. No behavioural change to `--auto`, `--seed`, `--bot`, `--bot-config`, `--json`, `--poll`, `--max-duration` or `balance-stats.json` on the clean path; the printed success lines are unchanged.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — wait loop, stop reasons, target-closed classification, interruption finaliser, `--help` block.
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts` *(new)* — the hermetic seam tests.
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts` — declarations for the new exports.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (reused, not modified).
- `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs`, `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` — pattern reference only.

## Notes

- Tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs (suite-write guard AH-0MVS9TY0N0034LZT); the suite never dirties the checkout.
- No new runtime dependency; node built-ins plus the already-imported Playwright/Vite modules only.
- Checkpoint-append tests (parent AC2(d)/(e)) land in child 2 with the checkpoint implementation; this child's test (a) asserts the routing, not the partial bytes. "Salvage path" in these ACs means this single rescue/finalise seam — the partial-writing branch it calls lands in child 2.
data.title: Interruption seam and hermetic crash-path tests

## Problem

`shared/tree_coverage.py` `run_coverage_review` / `apply_coverage_review` compare a parent's acceptance criteria against the ACs of **every direct child**, including children auto-created by the `triage` skill from a boilerplate `[test-failure]` template ("the test passes on latest dev", "all related documentation is updated", "full project test suite passes").

When such a triage child is re-parented under the hardening item that actually owns the flake (the documented triage practice), the parent can never reach `stage: plan_complete`: the template ACs do not textually match the parent's ACs, so the review returns `recommendation: "stop"` and the plan skill is required to leave the item `open` without advancing the stage.

Observed on AH-0MVWCFS7K000RIWI (2026-10-31): coverage 0 %, three unresolved conflicts on AC1/AC2/AC4, both children the triage template (AH-0MVWNIP0G002ZHOU critical, AH-0MVWJOH9T0006R1E medium). The same shape will be hit by every hardening/flake item that acquires reparented triage children.

## Expected behaviour

The coverage gate should treat auto-generated triage children differently from plan-generated feature children — e.g. exclude children tagged `test-failure` (or otherwise identified as triage-generated) from AC-coverage comparison, or exclude closed children, or allow an explicit "coverage credit" declaration on the parent mapping a child to a parent AC.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A parent work item whose only children are triage-generated `[test-failure]` items can reach `stage: plan_complete` without the coverage review returning `stop`.
- AC2 — Genuine plan-generated feature children are still coverage-checked exactly as today (no weakening of the gate for real decompositions).
- AC3 — Unit tests in `skills/shared/tests` cover: triage-only children (proceed), mixed triage + feature children (feature children still evaluated), and closed children.
- AC4 — `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` (or the relevant plan/triage docs) records the rule and its rationale.

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MVWCFS7K000RIWI (plan run blocked by this gate)
- Evidence precedent: AH-0MVWDOOY6004HF4W closed as a duplicate of the same hardening item.

## Plan review (plan skill, auto-complete path)

Auto-complete path taken: effort **Extra Small** / risk **Low** (below the
autoplan threshold), so **no child features were created**. This item is a
single minimal end-to-end slice: helper change, unit tests, documentation note.

### Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — AC coverage review (`run_coverage_review`, `compute_coverage`, `resolve_coverage_gaps`, `apply_coverage_review`); the triage exemption belongs here.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — existing unit-test suite for the helper.
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — canonical triage child creation; sets `--tags test-failure`, `--issue-type bug`, `--stage intake_complete` (this is the marker an exemption can key on).
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — plan-skill implementation reference; record the rule and its rationale here.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — plan-skill operational brief (AC coverage review step).
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — triage skill brief (re-parenting practice).

The helper, its tests and the referenced doc live in the **SorraAgents**
framework repo (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`), not
in the AI_Hell game repo.

### Implementation assumptions

- The exemption keys on the `test-failure` tag set by the triage script; the
  `[test-failure]` title prefix is not used as the primary signal.
- Exempt (triage-tagged) children are excluded from the AC comparison but stay
  visible in the review output (reported as excluded) so the audit trail is
  preserved; `coverage` is computed from the remaining children only.
- When every direct child is exempt, coverage is vacuously complete and the
  review recommends `proceed` (AC1).
- Tag-less children keep today's behaviour exactly (AC2): same Jaccard
  thresholds (0.4 coverage, 0.2 auto-close floor), same `stop` semantics.
- Test-first: write the three AC3 unit tests first (red), then implement the
  exemption (green).

### Verification

- AC1 — unit test with a stubbed `wl` runner whose only children carry `tags: ["test-failure"]`; assert `run_coverage_review` returns `recommendation: "proceed"` and `apply_coverage_review(target_stage="plan_complete")` advances the stage.
- AC2 — existing coverage tests keep asserting tag-less children are compared and still produce `stop` when their ACs do not match.
- AC3 — `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` gains the three cases: triage-only (proceed), mixed triage + feature (feature children still evaluated), closed children (documented behaviour per the OPEN QUESTION below).
- AC4 — `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` gains a section stating the rule, the `test-failure` marker and the rationale: re-parented triage children must not block `plan_complete`, while genuine decompositions stay gated.
- Suite run via `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc pytest).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was conducted: this was a downtime-dispatched
auto-complete plan run (effort Extra Small / risk Low, below the planning
threshold), so the plan proceeded on the documented assumptions above.

- OPEN QUESTION (directed to Producer; non-blocking) — AC3 requires a unit test
  for "closed children" but does not state the expected outcome. Recommended
  default: a closed child is exempt **only** when it is also tagged
  `test-failure`; a closed tag-less feature child keeps taking part in the
  coverage comparison exactly as today (conservative — exempting all closed
  children would let a parent pass the gate by closing an uncovered feature
  child). The AC3 "closed children" test will assert this default explicitly,
  so a later decision is a one-line change. Why it matters: the alternative
  (exclude every closed child) weakens the gate for real decompositions.

### Plan changelog

- 2026-11-01 — plan skill (auto-complete path): added Key Files, implementation
  assumptions, verification map, Appendix and this changelog; no child items
  created (below planning threshold); stage advanced `intake_complete` →
  `plan_complete`.

# Teleport: 60 s recharge, no charge stack, pickup refreshes to ready

## Problem statement

Teleport currently regenerates far too quickly — **15 s at base, 5 s at the
upgrade cap** — and stockpiles up to **3 stored warps**, so a permanently owned
Teleport is almost always available and the defensive escape costs the player
nothing. Teleport should become a **single, slow-recharging escape**: one charge
every **60 s** at base (scaling to **20 s** at the upgrade cap), with a run-time
Teleport pickup refreshing the timer to ready immediately, and **no stored-charge
bookkeeping** at all.

## Users

- **As a player** who has just teleported out of danger, I want the escape to be
  gone for about a minute, so that evading a threat has a real cost and the
  ability is a decision rather than a permanent safety net.
- **As a player** flying through a Teleport drop while my Teleport is recharging,
  I want that pickup to make it ready again immediately, so chasing the drop is
  worth the risk.
- **As a player** who has permanently added Teleport to a loadout slot, I do not
  want to be offered a redundant "Teleport Charge" in the hold-full choice or
  see a Teleport wedge on the mini-boss wheel, because there is no charge left
  to grant.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the new model expressed as catalogue/level data
  and one shared seam, so the game and every gym cannot drift.

## Desired behaviour

1. **No charge stack.** Teleport has no stored-count, no FIFO pool and no cap-3
   counter. Its state is binary: **ready** (recharge timer 0) or **recharging**
   (timer > 0). The `teleportStacks` level axis is retired.
2. **Recharge interval.** Spending Teleport starts one recharge timer of the
   level-derived interval: **60 s at level 1 (base) → 20 s at the upgrade cap**
   (same 3:1 base:cap ratio and `k = 0.3` curve shape as today, applied to the
   new numbers). The axis stays charges-per-second (`base 1/60`, `cap 1/20`) so
   the monotonic non-decreasing rate contract holds.
3. **Pickup sets the timer to 0.** A run-time Teleport pickup makes Teleport
   **ready immediately** (recharge timer reset to 0), including while it is
   mid-recharge, on top of its existing temporary-level effect.
4. **Hold-full reward readies it.** A hold-full Teleport reward (which grants
   permanent ownership, i.e. a loadout slot) also leaves Teleport ready
   (timer 0).
5. **Usable only while held.** Teleport is available while it is held — either
   through an active temporary field-pickup level or through permanent
   ownership — and unavailable once a temporary window expires without
   permanent ownership (existing rule for unowned kinds).
6. **Rewards retire once permanently owned.** Once Teleport is permanently owned
   it is **excluded from the hold-full choice pool and the mini-boss wheel** —
   no `power-up-charge` offer, no wheel wedge, and no `+1 level` bonus grant for
   it. While it is *not* permanently owned it is still offered as a base
   `★ New` entry, which grants the slot.
7. **Auto-defence tie-break.** When both Phase Shift (charges > 0) and Teleport
   (ready) are available, the shared resolver picks **50/50** from the injected
   rng, regardless of Phase Shift's charge count. Only one available → that one;
   neither → nothing.
8. **HUD.** The Teleport row shows `ready` when the timer is 0 and
   `next in Ns` while recharging, with no stack suffix; the row greys out while
   recharging. Same HUD in the game and every gym.
9. **Gym↔game parity.** All of the above lives in shared code
   (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`,
   `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`); `PlayScene` and every gym inherit it. No
   gym override, no divergent copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single-use model.** Teleport exposes no stored-charge count anywhere
  (no `teleportStacks` axis, no FIFO pool, no `POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP` special case
  for `teleport`); the store/registry report `ready` / `recharging` plus a
  remaining-seconds value. Verified by unit tests over `PowerUpLevelStore` and
  `EffectsRegistry`, and by the removal of the `teleportStacks` spec axis.
- **AC2 — Recharge interval 60 s → 20 s.** `teleportRechargeTime()` returns
  **60 s at level 1** and **20 s at the upgrade cap**, and is monotonically
  non-increasing across levels. Tested at the endpoints plus a monotonicity
  sweep.
- **AC3 — Spending starts the timer.** An automatic danger activation consumes
  the ready Teleport and starts one level-derived recharge timer; while the
  timer runs the ability is unavailable so no second warp can fire. Test:
  spend → unavailable → `tick(interval − ε)` still unavailable →
  `tick(+ε)` ready.
- **AC4 — Pickup (and hold-full reward) sets the timer to 0.** Collecting a
  Teleport drop while mid-recharge makes it ready immediately; a hold-full
  Teleport grant also leaves it ready. Tested for a field pickup during a
  cooldown and for the hold-full grant path.
- **AC5 — Rewards retire once permanently owned.** A permanently-owned Teleport
  produces no hold-full choice option (no `power-up-charge`) and no mini-boss
  wheel wedge, while an unowned Teleport is still offered as a `★ New` base
  entry. The exclusion is driven by catalogue data, never an
  `id === 'teleport'` branch. Tests cover both builders.
- **AC6 — Auto-defence tie-break is 50/50.** When both abilities are available
  the resolver returns `phase_shift` / `teleport` with equal probability from
  the injected rng, independent of Phase Shift's charge count; single-ability
  and neither-available cases unchanged. Seeded determinism tested.
- **AC7 — HUD reflects the new model.** The Teleport row renders `ready` /
  `next in Ns` (no stack count) and greys out while recharging, in `PlayScene`
  and in every gym that shows the shared HUD.
- **AC8 — Gym↔game parity holds.** The change is implemented once in shared
  code with no gym-specific override; the parity/equivalence suites
  (`src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) pass with the new model.
- **AC9 — Documentation updated.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 bullet,
  the teleport catalogue row, the §4.4.3 level table), `docs/BALANCING.md`, the
  catalogue description in `src/powerups/types.ts` and the code comments in
  `powerUpLevels.ts` / `effects.ts` / `choice.ts` all describe the single-use
  60 s → 20 s model; the `src/powerUpLevelingDocs.test.ts` assertions are
  updated to match.
- **AC10 — Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (run through the test skill / dev-push gate), and every new behaviour above
  is covered by a test that would fail if the behaviour regressed.

## Constraints

- **Data-only tuning** (producer answer Q3 = A): change the level-spec axis and
  the shared seams; do **not** add a runtime/rules-config knob for the recharge
  interval. Live gym tuning sliders stay with AH-0MV82IAYG000WS8B.
- **Phase Shift is out of scope** — it keeps its charge pool and its 30 s → 10 s
  recharge. The shared charge-pool machinery must stay intact for Shield, Thorn
  Field, Phase Shift, Force Field and Mystery UFO.
- **No new offer kind** and no `id === 'teleport'` special case: express the
  model as catalogue data (a flag/axis that says "single-use, no charge pool,
  not rewardable when owned") so the shared builders stay kind-agnostic.
- **No new per-scene counters**: the recharge timer must live in the one
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (already ticked by the shared effect path).
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `teleportRechargeRate` axis
  (`base: 1/15`, `cap: 1/5`, `k: 0.3`) → `teleportRechargeTime()` 15 s → 5 s;
  `teleportStacks` axis (`base: 1`, `cap: 3`, `k: 0.5`); `_poolCap()` special-cases
  `phase_shift`/`teleport` to `POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP`; per-charge timers in
  `_rechargeTimers` advanced by `tickRecharge()`; `consumeTeleport()`,
  `teleportStacks()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`, `consumableRechargeRemaining()`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `selectAutoDefence(phaseCharges, teleportStacks, rng)`
  compares available counts (greater count wins, exact tie → 50/50);
  `EffectsRegistry.consumeTeleport()`, `hasTeleport()`, `teleportStacks()`,
  `updateDanger()`/`_advanceAutoDefence` and the HUD snapshot builder
  (`stacks: teleportStacks`).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (~1105) — `registry.consumeTeleport()` in the
  shared `triggerTeleport` path, consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `buildChargeOption()` produces
  `"+1 charge, regenerates every N s"` for an owned consumable;
  `buildOwnedPowerUpOffer()` dispatches on the catalogue `consumable` flag;
  `buildChoiceCandidates()` applies the six-slot gate.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` — `isWheelKind()` / `orderedOwnedKinds()` /
  `buildWheelWedges()` build wedges from the shared `ownedIds`, and the bonus
  wedge grants `+1 level` on every owned kind.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Teleport row shows the stack count plus `next in Ns`
  (`buildHUDLabel`, `_powerUpRecharge`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` lines 319, 1175, 1210, 1549 and
  `docs/BALANCING.md` (recharge/charge tables) document 15 s → 5 s and the
  cap-3 pool.
- Tests pinning today's numbers: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` (958,
  1043, 1072, 1139, 1525, 1730), `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (1196–1233,
  2412, 2613, 2631), `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` (660), `src/powerUpLevelingDocs.test.ts`
  (74).

## Desired change

Retire the Teleport charge stack and replace it with a single readiness timer
whose interval is 60 s at base and 20 s at the upgrade cap; make any Teleport
pickup (and the hold-full grant) reset that timer to 0; exclude a
permanently-owned Teleport from the hold-full choice and the mini-boss wheel;
and simplify the shared auto-defence tie-break to a uniform 50/50 whenever both
abilities are available. The charge-pool machinery stays for the other five
consumables.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — replace `teleportStacks` with a single-use
  readiness API; retune `teleportRechargeRate` to `1/60 → 1/20`; drop the
  teleport `POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP` branch in `_poolCap()`.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — catalogue entry: single-use Teleport (no charge
  pool, not rewardable when owned) + updated player-facing description.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `consumeTeleport()` → start timer; pickup/hold-full
  grant resets the timer to 0; `selectAutoDefence` becomes readiness-based with
  a 50/50 tie; HUD snapshot stops publishing a stack count.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — owned-Teleport offer suppressed via catalogue data.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` — owned-Teleport excluded from wedges and from
  the bonus `+1 level` grant.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — `ready` / `next in Ns` row without a stack suffix.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — confirm the shared `triggerTeleport` path
  consumes the single readiness (no per-scene counter).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md` — rules and tables.
- Tests: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/choice*.test.ts`, `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.test.ts`,
  `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/powerUpLevelingDocs.test.ts`, gym suites that exercise Teleport.

## Related work

- Gym recharge-time tuning sliders (recharge follow-up) (AH-0MV82IAYG000WS8B) —
  open; live gym sliders for Phase/Teleport recharge. Not required here, but the
  slider must be re-pointed at the new single-use interval when it lands.
- Checkpoint does not persist consumable charge pools (AH-0MVY3IGRC00954UD) —
  open; with no charge stack the **recharge timer becomes the entire Teleport
  state**, so a checkpoint resume must restore it or a resumed run gets a free
  teleport.
- Teleport and Phase Shift should recharge (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR) — completed;
  introduced the recharging pool this item replaces for Teleport.
- Consumable upgrades should not be endless (AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW) — completed;
  the level-derived cap/interval model being retuned here.
- Timed consumable field pickups should use the absorbed-hit model
  (AH-0MVUVSW4J0009QUW) — completed; the `regenRequiresOwnership` flag that
  distinguishes owned from pickup-only consumables.
- Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC) — completed;
  introduced the shared auto-defence resolver whose tie-break AC6 changes.
- Description of teleport is wrong (AH-0MVBKQAKU004NQ77) — completed; prior
  player-facing copy correction (expect the same doc surfaces to change again).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Auto-defence behaviour change.** Today the ability with the greater available
  count wins, so 3 Phase charges beat a stored Teleport. Producer answer Q3 = C
  makes it a uniform 50/50 whenever both are available — an intentional
  behaviour change that must be recorded in the GDD and pinned by a seeded test.
- **Test churn.** Roughly a dozen assertions pin 15 s / 5 s, the stack count or
  the greater-count tie-break; they must be rewritten to the new model rather
  than deleted.
- **Checkpoint gap.** A checkpoint written before the timer is persisted can
  resume with a ready Teleport it had already spent (AH-0MVY3IGRC00954UD). If
  that item has not landed, record the gap explicitly and keep the restore path
  honest (a restored permanent Teleport starts ready, which is the least
  surprising option).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Retiring charges for *all* consumables, retuning Phase
  Shift, or adding live tuning sliders are out of scope — record them as linked
  work items, not extra scope here.
- **Assumption:** a pickup while Teleport is already ready is a harmless no-op
  (it sets the timer to 0, which it already is) and still refreshes the
  temporary level window.
- **Assumption:** "usable only while held" keeps today's unowned-kind rule; no
  new ownership semantics are introduced.
- **Assumption:** the AI bot/eval code paths consume Teleport only through the
  shared registry (`canTeleport()`), so no separate bot change is expected — to
  be confirmed during implementation.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q: Does 60 s apply flat at every level, or is 60 s the base with a shorter
  levelled cap?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(b) 60 s base with a
  level-derived cap.** Follow-up Q: what is the cap? — Answer: **(a) 60 s → 20 s**
  (keeps today's 3:1 base:cap ratio and the `k = 0.3` curve shape).

- **Q: What does a hold-full Teleport reward do now that there are no charges?**

## Goal

Make the Teleport recharge interval **60 s at base → 20 s at the upgrade cap**
in the power-up level catalogue and retire the `teleportStacks` axis, so the
level data describes a **single-use** escape instead of a 3-deep charge stack.

Parent: Teleport regenerates too quickly (AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4) — covers parent
**AC1** (single-use model, data half) and **AC2** (60 s → 20 s).

## User story

As a maintainer, I want the recharge interval and the "no charge stack" rule
expressed as catalogue/level data, so the game and every gym resolve the same
numbers and no seam needs an `id === 'teleport'` special case.

## Scope

- `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.teleport`: delete the `teleportStacks` spec entry and
  remove the `teleportStacks` variable from `PowerUpLevelStats`, the
  levelled-variable list and `CONSUMABLE_CHARGE_CAP_AXES`.
- Retune `teleportRechargeRate` to `base: 1/60`, `cap: 1/20`, `k: 0.3`
  (charges/second, so the monotonic non-decreasing rate contract holds) and
  rewrite the `rationale` beside the numbers (today it explains 15 s → 5 s).
- Replace the retired cap axis with **catalogue data**: a single-use kind's
  charge cap is `1` expressed as a flag on the spec/catalogue entry (e.g.
  `singleUse: true`), never an `id === 'teleport'` branch, so
  `resolveConsumableChargeCap('teleport', n) === 1` at every level.
- Update the module docstring blocks that state "Teleport — cap 3 and the
  shipped `teleportRechargeRate` (15 s → 5 s)" and the stack-reconciliation
  note that counts "Teleport stored teleports".

Out of scope: the store readiness API (child 2), the pickup/hold-full reset
(child 3), the auto-defence ranking (child 4), the reward surfaces (child 5),
the HUD (child 6) and the documentation sweep (child 7). Do **not** retune
Phase Shift (30 s → 10 s and cap 3 stay as they are).

## Implementation approach (tests first)

1. Write the failing specs in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`:
   `teleportRechargeTime()` is 60 at level 1 and 20 at the upgrade cap; a
   monotonic non-increasing sweep across levels 1..cap; `teleportStacks` is gone
   from the specs/stats; `resolveConsumableChargeCap('teleport', n) === 1`.
2. Change the data, then make the specs pass.
3. Rewrite (do not delete) the assertions that pin 15 s / 5 s or the cap-3
   teleport pool in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` (~lines 958, 1043,
   1072, 1139, 1525, 1730).
4. Run changed-scope tests through the test skill (`/skill:test`) — never an
   ad-hoc `npx vitest`.

## Definition of done

- The catalogue resolves 60 s → 20 s with a monotonically non-increasing
  interval, and the single-use cap is data-driven.
- No `teleportStacks` axis or stats field remains and no `POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP`
  branch mentions teleport in the data layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `teleportRechargeTime()` resolves **60 s** at level 1 and
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel('teleport', 0).teleportRechargeRate === 1/60`.
- AC2 — At the upgrade cap `teleportRechargeTime()` resolves **20 s**, and a
  monotonicity sweep asserts the interval is non-increasing across every level.
- AC3 — The `teleportStacks` spec axis, its `PowerUpLevelStats` field and every
  reference are removed; no test pins a cap-3 teleport pool any more.
- AC4 — The single-use charge cap (`1` at every level) is derived from
  catalogue/spec data with no `id === 'teleport'` branch, asserted by

- AC5 — Phase Shift's axes are unchanged (30 s → 10 s, cap 3), asserted by its

## Goal

Make `PowerUpLevelStore` expose Teleport as a **single readiness state** —
`ready` or `recharging` plus a remaining-seconds value — where spending starts
one level-derived recharge timer and no stored-count/FIFO bookkeeping exists
anywhere.

Parent: Teleport regenerates too quickly (AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4) — covers parent
**AC1** (runtime half) and **AC3** (spending starts the timer).

## User story

As a player who has just teleported out of danger, I want the escape to be gone
for about a minute, so evading a threat has a real cost.

## Scope

- Replace `teleportStacks()` and the per-charge teleport pool with a readiness
  view: `hasTeleport()` (ready), `isTeleportRecharging()`, and
  `teleportRechargeRemaining()` (seconds, 0 when ready).
- `consumeTeleport()` spends the single ready use and starts **one** timer of
  the level-derived `teleportRechargeTime()`; while the timer runs the ability
  is unavailable, so no second warp can fire.
- `tickRecharge(dt)` clears that timer at 0 and returns the kind to ready.
- Remove the `teleport` branch from `_poolCap()` (`POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP` stays
  for Phase Shift only) while keeping the shared charge-pool machinery intact
  for Shield, Thorn Field, Phase Shift, Force Field and Mystery UFO.
- `EffectsRegistry` projects the same state (`hasTeleport`, `isTeleportReady`,
  `teleportRechargeRemaining`, `teleportRechargeTime`) and its HUD snapshot
  stops publishing a `stacks` count for teleport.
- Confirm the shared `CombatScene.triggerTeleport` path consumes the readiness
  with no per-scene counter (expected: no change beyond the accessor name).
- Keep the store as the **only** home of the timer.
- Confirm the AI bot/eval paths consume Teleport only through the shared boolean
  gates (`CombatScene.canTeleport()` → `registry.hasTeleport()`), so no bot
  change is expected; if a caller reads the stack count, update it to the
  readiness view in this child.

Out of scope: the pickup/hold-full reset (child 3), the auto-defence ranking
(child 4), the reward surfaces (child 5) and the HUD row rendering (child 6).

## Implementation approach (tests first)

1. Failing tests in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`: spend → not ready →
   `tick(interval − ε)` still not ready → `tick(+ε)` ready, with
   `teleportRechargeRemaining()` decreasing; a second `consumeTeleport()` while
   recharging returns `false`.
2. Failing tests in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` for the registry projection,
   replacing the assertions at ~1196–1233, 2412, 2613 and 2631 that pin the
   FIFO stack count.
3. Implement, then verify by grep that no scene holds a teleport counter.
4. Run changed-scope tests through the test skill.

## Definition of done

- Teleport state is binary, its timer is level-derived, and a spent Teleport
  cannot fire twice inside one interval.
- No stored-count/FIFO API remains for teleport in the store or the registry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Single-use model.** Teleport exposes no stored-charge count anywhere
  (no `teleportStacks` axis, no FIFO pool, no `POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP` special case
  for `teleport`); the store/registry report `ready` / `recharging` plus a
  remaining-seconds value, verified by unit tests over `PowerUpLevelStore` and
  `EffectsRegistry`.
- AC2 — **Spending starts the timer.** An automatic danger activation consumes
  the ready Teleport and starts one level-derived recharge timer; while the
  timer runs the ability is unavailable so no second warp can fire. Test: spend
  → unavailable → `tick(interval − ε)` still unavailable → `tick(+ε)` ready.
- AC3 — A second `consumeTeleport()` while the timer runs returns `false`.
- AC4 — `teleportRechargeRemaining()` reports the remaining seconds and 0 when
  ready; nothing in the store or the registry surfaces a teleport stack/FIFO
  count.
- AC5 — `_poolCap()` no longer special-cases teleport (`POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP`
  remains only for Phase Shift); the other five consumables' pool behaviour is
  unchanged, asserted by their existing suites.
- AC6 — The recharge timer lives only in `PowerUpLevelStore` and advances only
  through `tickRecharge` (the shared `EffectsRegistry.tick` call site); no scene
  keeps a teleport counter.
- AC7 — A restored permanent Teleport (checkpoint replay through the shared
  grant seam) starts **ready**; record this as the documented default for the
  open checkpoint gap AH-0MVY3IGRC00954UD.
- AC8 — No bot/eval path reads a teleport stack count; the readiness view is the
  only consumption API (`canTeleport()` / `hasTeleport()` are boolean already).
- AC9 — Changed-scope tests pass through the test skill.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`
- `src/powerups/effects.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Child 1 — Spec axis: single-use Teleport recharge (60 s → 20 s)

## Goal

Retire Teleport from the **reward surfaces** once it is permanently owned: no
`power-up-charge` option in the hold-full choice, no mini-boss wheel wedge and
no `+1 level` bonus grant — while an unowned Teleport is still offered as a
base `★ New` entry that grants the slot.

Parent: Teleport regenerates too quickly (AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4) — covers parent
**AC5** (rewards retire once permanently owned).

## User story

As a player who has permanently added Teleport to a loadout slot, I do not want
to be offered a redundant "Teleport Charge" or see a Teleport wedge on the
mini-boss wheel, because there is no charge left to grant.

## Scope

- Catalogue data: add a flag to `PowerUpEntry` in `src/powerups/types.ts` (e.g.
  `rewardableWhenOwned?: boolean`, defaulting to `true`; Teleport opts out) and
  a derived helper (e.g. `isRewardableWhenOwned(id)`) so no builder branches on
  the id. Document the flag beside the existing `consumable` /
  `regenRequiresOwnership` / `availableWhenSlotsFull` flags.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts`: `buildOwnedPowerUpOffer` /
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions` produce no option for a permanently-owned kind
  whose entry opts out of owned rewards. `buildChoiceCandidates` must still
  offer an **unowned** Teleport as its base `★ New` entry (six-slot gate
  unchanged).
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`: `isWheelKind` / `orderedOwnedKinds` exclude
  an owned non-rewardable kind, so it gets no wedge and the bonus wedge grants
  no level to it; the `applyMineralChoiceReward` path is untouched.
- Keep the 1.35× owned-offer weight and the option-kind vocabulary unchanged —
  no new offer kind.

Out of scope: the store/registry readiness API (child 2) and the HUD (child 6).

## Implementation approach (tests first)

1. Failing tests in `src/powerups/choice.test.ts` (and the choice suite that
   covers `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`): a permanently-owned Teleport yields no
   `power-up-charge` option, while a permanently-owned Shield/Phase Shift still
   yields one; an unowned Teleport is still present as a base-pool entry.
2. Failing tests in `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts`:
   `buildWheelWedges` has no teleport wedge for an owned Teleport and
   `drawWheelOutcome(0, …)` (the bonus slot) grants it no level; unowned kinds
   and other consumables are unaffected.
3. Assert the exclusion is catalogue-driven: a source assertion that no builder
   compares `id === 'teleport'` for reward gating (mirror the existing
   kind-agnostic source assertions in those suites).
4. Run changed-scope tests through the test skill.

## Definition of done

- An owned Teleport produces no reward options on either surface, driven only by
  catalogue data, and the unowned base entry still works.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Rewards retire once permanently owned.** A permanently-owned Teleport
  produces no hold-full choice option (no `power-up-charge`) and no mini-boss
  wheel wedge, while an unowned Teleport is still offered as a `★ New` base
  entry. The exclusion is driven by catalogue data, never an
  `id === 'teleport'` branch. Tests cover both builders.
- AC2 — `buildWheelWedges` / `orderedOwnedKinds` give an owned Teleport no wedge
  and `drawWheelOutcome` grants it no `+1 level` bonus.
- AC3 — `buildChoiceCandidates` still surfaces an unowned Teleport as its base
  `★ New` entry, and the six-slot gate is unchanged.
- AC4 — Other consumables (Shield, Thorn Field, Phase Shift, Force Field,
  Mystery UFO) are unaffected: each still yields its charge offer and wheel
  wedge when owned, asserted by their existing suites.
- AC5 — The exclusion is a documented catalogue entry flag plus a derived
  helper, with a source assertion that no builder compares `id === 'teleport'`;
  no new offer kind is introduced.
- AC6 — Changed-scope tests pass through the test skill.

- `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts`

# Unit tests for resolveCountdownFraction helper

## Goal
Write comprehensive unit tests for the pure `resolveCountdownFraction` helper function before it is implemented. These tests must fail initially (red).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Test coverage of all four countdown sources.** Tests cover the four sources: consumable recharge (arriving), power-up timed window (expiring), weapon field-pickup window (expiring), and permanent Orbital Strike cadence (arriving).
- **AC2 — Edge cases at 0, 1, zero total, and undefined total.** Tests verify correct behaviour at fraction boundaries (remaining=0, remaining=total) and when total is zero or undefined.
- **AC3 — Monotonicity for arriving mode.** Tests verify fraction rises monotonically as remaining increases toward total.
- **AC4 — Monotonicity for expiring mode.** Tests verify fraction decreases monotonically as remaining decreases toward zero.
- **AC5 — Deterministic output.** The function is pure — same inputs always yield same output, no clock dependency.

## Implementation notes (for the implementer)
- Function signature: `resolveCountdownFraction({ remaining, total, mode: 'arriving'|'expiring' }): number`
- Arriving mode: `fraction = remaining / total` (0 → 1 as wait elapses)
- Expiring mode: `fraction = remaining / total` (1 → 0 as window burns down)
- Guard: if total ≤ 0 or undefined, return 0.
- Module: `src/ui/hudCountdown.ts` (new file).

## Key Files
- `src/ui/hudCountdown.test.ts` — unit tests (created first)
- `src/ui/hudCountdown.ts` — implementation (created after tests pass)

## Goal

Restore **hardware-GPU access for the frame-time harness on the reference host**, so AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P (hardware-GPU desktop verification) can record the two runs its acceptance criteria require. This is an **operator/machine task**: every step needs `sudo`, a re-login or physical access, so it cannot be completed by an agent session.

**User story:** As the producer, I want the reference host to expose a working hardware GPU driver to the measuring user, so the 60 FPS desktop target can be measured on a real GPU instead of a software rasteriser.

## Measured state (2026-11-04, commit `da8aaa8f`, host `rgardler` reference machine)

The host **does** have GPU hardware: `lspci` shows `NVIDIA GA107M [GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Mobile]` (01:00.0) and `AMD Renoir [Radeon Vega Series]` (06:00.0); `nvidia_uvm`/`nvidia_drm`/`amdgpu` are loaded. Two independent, separately fixable faults stop the harness from using either one as a WebGL backend.

### 1. NVIDIA: kernel module and userspace driver disagree (MOOT until reboot)

- `nvidia-smi` → `Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch` (`NVML library version: 595.99`).
- `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` → `NVRM version: ... 595.91.07` (kernel module), while the installed userspace is `nvidia-driver-595-open 595.99.02-0ubuntu0.26.04.1`; the host has been up 2 days 23 h, so the module predates the last driver upgrade.
- The device nodes themselves are **not** the problem: `/dev/nvidia0`, `/dev/nvidiactl`, `/dev/nvidia-uvm` and `/dev/nvidia-modeset` are mode `666` and open successfully as the non-root measuring user.
- A mismatched kernel/userspace pair cannot create a GL or Vulkan context, so `--gpu` cannot reach the RTX 3050 Ti in this state even though the nodes are writable.
- **Fix:** reboot (loads the matching 595.99 module set), or reload the module without a reboot (`sudo systemctl stop gdm` then `sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia`), then confirm `nvidia-smi` reports the GPU.

### 2. AMD iGPU: DRM render nodes are not accessible to the measuring user

- `/dev/dri/renderD128` (Renoir, 06:00.0), `/dev/dri/renderD129` (NVIDIA), `card0`, `card1` are `root:video` / `root:render`, mode `660`, with an ACL granting only `gdm-greeter`.
- `uid=1000(rgardler)` groups: `adm, cdrom, sudo, dip, plugdev, users, lpadmin, lxd` — **not** `video` or `render`. Opening any of the four nodes fails with `EACCES` (`Permission denied`), so Mesa/radv/ANGLE cannot enumerate a hardware device.
- **Fix (either):** `sudo usermod -aG video,render rgardler` then fully re-login (group membership is per-session); **or** run the measurement from the graphical seat session, where logind grants the seat user the device ACL.

### 3. No display server, and Electron is no longer installed

- `DISPLAY` is unset and there is no Xorg/Xvfb, so a *windowed* hardware run needs a seat. This does not block the measurements themselves: `--ozone-platform=headless` (Electron) and headless Chromium both work, and the harness's window-visibility guard covers the Electron case.
- `node_modules/electron` is **absent** in the main checkout, so `--host electron` stops with "Electron is not installed" — even the software Electron row is currently not reproducible here. `electron` is an `optionalDependencies` entry, so a plain `npm install` prunes it again; install it explicitly (`npm install electron@^45.2.2`) before the Electron runs.

### Harness guard re-verified (both desktop hosts, short guard-check runs)

| Invocation | Result |
|---|---|
| `--gpu --require-hardware-webgl --scene GymPerformance --seconds 3 --warmup 1` | exit 1: *"Refusing to publish a hardware-GPU baseline: the page rendered on a software WebGL backend (ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver))"* |
| `--host electron --gpu --require-hardware-webgl ...` | exit 1: *"Electron is not installed, so `--host electron` cannot run."* |

So the guard behaves correctly: it refuses to publish a software run as a desktop hardware baseline. The gap is host access, not harness behaviour.

## Scope

- Bring up a working hardware GPU backend for the measuring user on the reference host (`nvidia-smi` reports the GPU; a Vulkan/GL context is creatable as `rgardler`; `/dev/dri/render*` openable or an equivalent working path).
- Install the (optional) `electron` dependency so `--host electron` can launch.
- Report back which driver path is available (NVIDIA proprietary vs AMD Mesa) and the renderer string a browser reports, so the verification run can be scheduled.

## Out of scope

- The verification runs themselves and the `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` records — they stay in AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P.
- Any optimisation work, harness change or target change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `nvidia-smi` (or an equivalent AMD/Mesa query) reports a GPU usable by the non-root measuring user, and the raw cause of the current fault (NVML driver/library mismatch / device-node `EACCES`) no longer applies.
2. `node_modules/electron` is installed and `npx electron --version` succeeds.
3. A headless Chromium launched with `--gpu` reports a **non-SwiftShader** `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` string (the string recorded in the completion comment) — i.e. `--require-hardware-webgl` passes.
4. The exact steps taken (commands, group/ACL changes, driver/reboot path) are recorded in a completion comment so the reference machine stays reproducible.

## Dependencies / related

- Blocks **AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P** (hardware-GPU desktop verification runs) via a dependency edge; discovered from it.
- Context: AH-0MW2DB9VN006XB63 (desktop host + Electron baseline, completed) and AH-0MVXV6VOI006P7VG (final verification) filed the gap this task unblocks.
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` § *Hardware-GPU desktop baseline (outstanding)* carries the same diagnosis and the fill-in commands.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P** – Hardware-GPU desktop verification runs for the 60 FPS target (browser + Electron) (blocked)
- **AH-0MW2DB9VN006XB63** – Desktop GPU and Electron renderer baseline is not measurable on this host (completed)
- **AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87** – Optimization pass (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — matched: 0mvxv6voi006p7vg, 0mw2db9vn006xb63, 0mw2iryj2006pv3p, 0x0000c0de, absent (+227 more)
- `README.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, access, acl, adm (+202 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absent, access, acl, adm, again (+184 more)


## Verified state after remediation (2026-11-04)

- **AC1 met.** `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` → 595.99.02 (was 595.91.07), `nvidia-smi` → GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU, driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2. Fixed **without a reboot** by stopping `nvidia-powerd` (it held 11 fds on `/dev/nvidia0`/`nvidiactl` and blocked `modprobe -r`) and reloading the module.

data.description:
## Goal

Make the frame-time harness's `--gpu` path actually reach a hardware WebGL backend, so `--require-hardware-webgl` can pass on the reference host now that AH-0MW2L3JXU008I2Z8 has restored the NVIDIA driver.

**User story:** As the producer, I want `measure-performance.mjs --gpu --require-hardware-webgl` to render on the real GPU on a hardware host, so the desktop 60 FPS target can be measured instead of being blocked by a SwiftShader refusal.

## Problem (measured, 2026-11-04, reference host, driver 595.99.02)

`rendererSwitches(gpu)` in `scripts/perf-launch.mjs` contributes only `--ignore-gpu-blocklist` and `--enable-gpu-rasterization` for a `--gpu` run. On this host Chromium still selects SwiftShader for those args alone; only an explicit ANGLE-Vulkan request reaches the GPU:

| Args | `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` |
|---|---|
| harness `--gpu` as-is | `ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)` |
| `+ --use-gl=angle --use-angle=vulkan` | `ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.329 (NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU (0x000025A0)), NVIDIA)` |
| `+ --use-angle=gl` / `+ --use-gl=egl` / `+ --enable-features=Vulkan` | SwiftShader |

Consequence: `node scripts/measure-performance.mjs --scene GymPerformance --seconds 3 --warmup 1 --gpu --require-hardware-webgl` exits 1 with the software-backend refusal on a host whose GPU is fully working.

## Desired change

Extend the `--gpu` switch set (`HARDWARE_SWITCHES` / `rendererSwitches()`) with the ANGLE-Vulkan pair so Chromium asks for the hardware backend, keeping the same switch set for the browser and Electron hosts (they share `rendererSwitches()`). Preserve the software path for runs without `--gpu` (SwiftShader must still be selectable so software baselines stay reproducible).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `rendererSwitches({ gpu: true })` includes the ANGLE-Vulkan selection, and `rendererSwitches({ gpu: false })` is unchanged — asserted in `scripts/perf-launch.test.ts`.
2. `node scripts/measure-performance.mjs --scene GymPerformance --seconds 3 --warmup 1 --gpu --require-hardware-webgl` exits 0 on the reference host and its JSON report carries a non-SwiftShader renderer string (the string recorded in the completion comment).
3. The change also applies to `--host electron` (shared `rendererSwitches()`), verified once `electron` is installed — or a comment records why it cannot be verified yet.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`'s hardware-GPU baseline section).
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Related

- Discovered from **AH-0MW2L3JXU008I2Z8** (host GPU access restored; AC3 needs this harness change).
- Blocks **AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P** (hardware-GPU desktop verification runs).

## Remediation performed on the reference host (2026-11-04, operator-driven)

Commands run by the producer in a sudo shell:

```bash
sudo usermod -aG video,render rgardler        # /etc/group: video:x:44:rgardler, render:x:990:rgardler
sudo systemctl stop gdm
sudo systemctl stop nvidia-powerd             # held 11 fds on /dev/nvidia0 + nvidiactl
sudo modprobe -r nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
```

No reboot was needed, so the in-flight `implement.py finish` runs and full test suites survived.

**Outcome:** `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` → `595.99.02` (was 595.91.07); `nvidia-smi` → `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU`, Driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2; module refcount 2. AC1 met.

**Diagnosis detail worth keeping:** the module could not be unloaded while `nvidia-powerd` (dynamic-boost daemon, `/dev/nvidia0` ×10 + `/dev/nvidiactl` ×1) held 11 file handles — the module refcount was exactly 11 with no `/sys/module/nvidia/holders` entry, so `fuser -v /dev/nvidia*` was the only way to find the holder.

## Chromium backend probe (the AC3 gap)

Probe matrix (Playwright 1.55.1 Chromium, harness `--gpu` arg set + one variant):

| Args | `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` |
|---|---|
| harness `--gpu` as-is (`--ignore-gpu-blocklist --enable-gpu-rasterization`) | `ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)` |
| `+ --use-gl=angle --use-angle=vulkan` | `ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.329 (NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU (0x000025A0)), NVIDIA)` |
| `+ --use-angle=gl`, `+ --use-gl=egl`, `+ --enable-features=Vulkan` | SwiftShader |

A real harness run (`node scripts/measure-performance.mjs --scene GymPerformance --seconds 3 --warmup 1 --gpu --require-hardware-webgl`) still exits 1 with the SwiftShader refusal, because `rendererSwitches()` in `scripts/perf-launch.mjs` never asks ANGLE for the Vulkan backend. **AC3 therefore cannot pass on this host without a harness change** — filed as a child work item (the harness change was originally out of scope; it is now required by AC3).

## Still outstanding in this item

- **AC2**: `node_modules/electron` still absent — `npm install electron@^45.2.2` (no sudo needed; belongs to the implement step, and will pick up the same renderer switch fix).
- **DRM/render-node access**: `usermod` is applied, but every current pi pane predates it and this host has no `sg`/`newgrp`, so the AMD/Mesa path is unverified. Not needed for the NVIDIA path (nodes are mode 666); it only becomes relevant if a fallback is ever wanted.
